legend: Mr. Chanek wants to knit a batik, a traditional cloth from Indonesia. The cloth forms a grid a%%ZSMJ0%% with size n×m%%ZSMJ1%%. There are k%%ZSMJ2%% colors, and each cell in the grid can be one of the k%%ZSMJ3%% colors.

Define a sub-rectangle as an ordered pair of two cells ((x1,y1),(x2,y2))%%ZSMJ4%%, denoting the top-left cell and bottom-right cell (inclusively) of a sub-rectangle in a%%ZSMJ5%%. Two sub-rectangles ((x1,y1),(x2,y2))%%ZSMJ6%% and ((x3,y3),(x4,y4))%%ZSMJ7%% have the same pattern if and only if the following holds:
for every pair (i,j)%%ZSMJ10%% where 0≤i≤x2−x1%%ZSMJ11%% and 0≤j≤y2−y1%%ZSMJ12%%, the color of cells (x1+i,y1+j)%%ZSMJ13%% and (x3+i,y3+j)%%ZSMJ14%% are equal.
Count the number of possible batik color combinations, such that the subrectangles ((ax,ay),(ax+r−1,ay+c−1))%%ZSMJ15%% and ((bx,by),(bx+r−1,by+c−1))%%ZSMJ16%% have the same pattern.
input: The first line contains five integers n%%ZSMJ18%%, m%%ZSMJ19%%, k%%ZSMJ20%%, r%%ZSMJ21%%, and c%%ZSMJ22%% (1≤n,m≤109%%ZSMJ23%%, 1≤k≤109%%ZSMJ24%%, 1≤r≤min%%ZSMJ25%%, 1 \leq c \leq \min(10^6, m)%%ZSMJ26%%) — the size of the batik, the number of colors, and size of the sub-rectangle.

The second line contains four integers a_x%%ZSMJ27%%, a_y%%ZSMJ28%%, b_x%%ZSMJ29%%, and b_y%%ZSMJ30%% (1 \leq a_x, b_x \leq n%%ZSMJ31%%, 1 \leq a_y, b_y \leq m%%ZSMJ32%%) — the top-left corners of the first and second sub-rectangle. Both of the sub-rectangles given are inside the grid (1 \leq a_x + r - 1%%ZSMJ33%%, b_x + r - 1 \leq n%%ZSMJ34%%, 1 \leq a_y + c - 1%%ZSMJ35%%, b_y + c - 1 \leq m%%ZSMJ36%%).
output: Output an integer denoting the number of possible batik color combinations modulo 10^9 + 7%%ZSMJ37%%.
